methods.label: Collect the terms containing b
methods.explanation:
To isolate \(b\), first remove the denominator and then gather every term containing \(b\). The original equation requires \(a-b\ne0\). Multiplying by this nonzero quantity gives
\[
m(a-b)=cab,
\]
so
\[
ma=mb+cab=b(m+ca).
\]
If \(m+ca\ne0\), division gives
\[
b=\frac{ma}{m+ca}.
\]
The original restriction \(b\ne a\) still applies. If this formula produces \(b=a\), that candidate must be rejected.

There is also a zero-coefficient case. If \(m+ca=0\), the equation becomes \(ma=0\). When \(ma\ne0\), there is no solution. When \(ma=0\), substituting \(m=-ca\) gives \(ca^2=0\), hence \(ca=m=0\). The original equation then holds for every \(b\ne a\). For example, \(a=1\) and \(c=m=0\) allow both \(b=0\) and \(b=2\), so \(b\) is not uniquely determined in this case.

Under the recorded convention of requesting an isolated expression, the answer is \(\boxed{b=\dfrac{ma}{m+ca}}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{D}}\), subject to the stated denominator restrictions. Choices A and B still contain \(b\) on the right and do not isolate it.
